We demonstrate the utility of NEUROSTRUCTURAL DECODING on three different tasks and on multiple language generation models. Evaluations show that automatically-derived structural constraints enforced by NEUROSTRUCTURAL DECODING improve generation performance on three distinct tasks: (i) a constrained text generation challenge, ; (ii) a mechanism summarization task, SuMe , (iii) a machine translation task from German to English .
outputs: Generated sentences that satisfy lexical and structural (syntactic) constraints
The outputs include coherent sentences using given concepts (COMMONGEN), mechanism summaries explaining biomedical relations (SuMe), and German-to-English translations (WMT19).
